title: automate-staged-proof-bundles-hashlink-anchoring-rollback-indexer
author: Nina Caldwell
description: Motivation: private deployments require cryptographically verifiable release artifacts plus a safe, reversible rollout mechanism. This PR introduces an automated pipeline to produce compact "proof bundles" (artifact + SBOM + cosign signature + minimal provenance metadata) and anchor them into a deterministic hashlink index used by the private installer and rollback tooling. Design: 1) CI step `ci/release/bundle-orchestrator` packages artifacts into a timestamped proof bundle and cosign-signs the envelope using an ephemeral KMS key. 2) A hashlink anchoring tool computes a compact merkle-like hashlink for the bundle and appends it to the release index in a way that preserves incremental attestability (index entries are content-addressed and signed). 3) The installer/upgrade controller consumes the anchored index and exposes a staged promotion workflow: 'canary -> staged -> promoted'. 4) A rollback-indexer service generates deterministic delta checkpoints (compact graph of bundle hashes + preflight checks) that the installer can apply atomically to revert to a previous promoted bundle. Backwards compatibility: index format supports legacy release entries and falls back to the previous index format if no hashlink is present. Implementation summary: - New Go tool `bundle-orchestrator` under `ci/release/bundle-orchestrator/` (packaging + cosign + anchor) with unit and integration tests. - New small Rust utility `hashlink-anchor` used in the pipeline for compact canonicalization (linux amd64 + arm64 builds). - Installer changes: Helm chart hooks in `installer/helm/templates/attest-hook.yaml` to validate proof bundles before upgrade; upgrade controller adaptations in `installer/controllers/upgrade.go` to support staged promotion and atomic rollback using the delta checkpoint format. - Terraform module `terraform/modules/kms-signing/` to provision ephemeral signing keys and IAM policies used in ephemeral CI jobs. - CI pipeline YAML `ci/pipelines/release-bundles.yaml` to wire steps and required secrets (KMS, cosign key refs, S3 buckets). Security and audit: bundles include SBOM (spdx+cyclonedx), cosign signatures, and the index commits are signed by the CI key and recorded in the release ledger for audit. Rollout plan: start with dry-run on private staging (off by default), promote to opt-in customers, then enable as default for new releases. Testing: end-to-end tests added under `test/e2e/release-bundles` exercising canary -> promote -> rollback scenarios. Checklist: - [x] bundle packaging and signing - [x] index anchoring - [x] installer preflight hook - [x] rollback checkpoint generator - [x] CI pipeline wiring - [x] docs/README and runbook - [x] e2e tests and perf smoke - [ ] run canary on staged cluster (followup controlled rollout).
